info.title: Kantel API
info.description: Kantel's public API for host apps, such as Lleverage, and for Kantel's own console, which uses it like any other client.

post.description: A link for an iframe: a watch-only live view of one of the session's open browsers, or a replay of one, open or closed. Needs viewer on the session; never an agent. The link carries a short-lived token scoped to that one view (never control), lasting `minutes`. A closed browser has no live view (`expired`); a deployment whose browsers keep no recordings has no replay (`unavailable`), and a recording past its retention is `expired`. Audited as `browser.session.embedded`, without the link.

parameters.name: browserSessionId
parameters.description: The browser session's ID, as the session's browser tool items name it.

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

post.description: Creates a project in the caller's organisation, which the `kantel-organisation` header names for a person in more than one. Needs an organisation-wide admin, or an organisation API key with the `create_projects` permission; a project key is refused, whatever its role. An organisation key holds its role on the new project at once. Audited as `identity.project.created`, with the caller as its actor.

get.description: The account's sandboxes the caller may see, newest first: by default the ones starting, running or stopping; `all` adds stopped, paused and errored ones. Deleted ones are left out. A key needs `sandboxes:read`.

parameters.name: account
parameters.description: The account to act in: the caller's personal account (the default for a person) or an organisation they belong to. An API key always acts in its own account, and naming another is `forbidden`.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: `starting`: being placed and booted. `running`: commands run now. `stopping`: its disk is being saved. `stopped`: no machine; its disk is kept as its newest snapshot, and running programs are gone. `paused`: like `stopped`, but its memory is kept too, so `resume` carries on where it left off (microVMs only). `error`: the last operation failed or the machine was lost; `recover` or `resume` it. `deleting`, `deleted`: erased for good, with its snapshots.

parameters.name: all
parameters.description: Include stopped, paused and errored sandboxes. Default: only active ones.

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

post.description: Makes a sandbox and starts it: an isolate unless `type` says `microvm`, from a snapshot when `from` names one. Answers as soon as it is placed (`starting`), or once it runs with `wait`. A full deployment is `exhausted`; no host able to run the type is `unavailable`. A key needs `sandboxes:write`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A key of your choosing, unique per call, such as a UUID. A retry with the same key gets the first call's answer and does nothing again. While the first call is still working, a retry may be `conflict`: retry it later.

put.description: Adds or changes a variable. A protected one needs at least one binding, and its value is kept encrypted and never shown again; leave `value` out to change only its bindings. A new value for a protected variable is a rotation: sandboxes keep their placeholders, and their next request carries the new value. Running sandboxes made from it pick the change up at once. Kantel's own names (`KANTEL_*`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY`, in any case) are refused. Protected values need the deployment's secrets key (`not_supported` without one). A key needs `account:admin`.

post.summary: Make a join token for one of your own hosts
post.description: A one-use token, shown once, and the one-line command that installs the host agent on a Linux machine and joins it to the account (the caller's personal account unless `account` names an organisation). The host dials out to this deployment and keeps the connection open, so it needs no inbound port. Once it has joined, the account's new sandboxes go on its own hosts, and no other account's sandboxes ever do. A key needs `account:admin`. Experimental: `not_supported` unless the deployment has turned account hosts on (`KANTEL_ACCOUNT_HOSTS`).

401.description: The request needs a valid credential (`unauthenticated`).

bearer.description: A host app's API key (`ktk_…`), from the API keys page or `POST /v1/keys`. It acts as a `service` actor, limited to its role and to the key's projects, or, for an organisation key, to its organisation. Behind Cloudflare Access a person's browser is signed in by Access instead, with no header.

Account.title: Account
Account.description: An account the caller may act in, with the caller's role in it.

accountId.description: The account the host joins: only its sandboxes will run there.

token.description: `kth_…`, shown once. It joins one host, once, before `expiresAt`.

command.description: The one-line command that installs the host agent on a Linux machine and joins it with the token. The host dials out to this deployment and keeps that connection open, so it needs no inbound port.

AccountKind.title: AccountKind
AccountKind.description: `personal`: one person's own account, made at their first sign-in; what they create is theirs alone unless they move it. `organisation`: an account people create or join, where sandboxes and snapshots are shared.

AccountLimits.title: AccountLimits
AccountLimits.description: The account's limits, where the deployment sets any.

prefix.description: The secret's first characters, such as `ksk_5n2p`, to tell keys apart.

sandboxIds.description: Limited to these sandboxes (and the ones it creates).

lastUsedAt.description: When the key last signed a call in, to within a minute. Absent until its first use.

ApiKey.title: ApiKey
ApiKey.description: A scoped API key. Its secret is never stored or shown after it is made.

ApiKeyPreset.title: ApiKeyPreset
ApiKeyPreset.description: A named set of scopes. `read-only`: the `:read` scopes. `agent`: what a coding agent needs to make and drive its own sandboxes, everything but `sandboxes:delete` and the account and host scopes. `ci`: `agent` plus `sandboxes:delete`. `admin`: every scope but `hosts:admin`.

ApiKeyScope.title: ApiKeyScope
ApiKeyScope.description: What a key may do. `sandboxes:read`: list and inspect sandboxes, their usage and events. `sandboxes:write`: create, change, start, stop, pause, resume, fork and recover. `sandboxes:delete`: delete for good. `exec`: run commands. `files`: read and write files. `access`: SSH, desktop, browser and public ports. `snapshots:read`, `snapshots:write`: snapshots and saved snapshots. `account:read`: the account, its members, keys, environments and sandboxes' egress. `account:admin`: members, keys, webhooks, telemetry, the proxy, environments and sandboxes' grants. `hosts:admin`: the deployment's hosts, for a super-admin's key only.

account.description: The account to act in: the caller's personal account (the default for a person) or an organisation they belong to. An API key always acts in its own account, and naming another is `forbidden`.

expiresInDays.description: Default 90. The key stops working after it.

ApproveDeviceLoginBody.title: ApproveDeviceLoginBody
ApproveDeviceLoginBody.description: The key the device gets, in the approver's personal account unless `account` names an organisation. Without `preset`, every scope the approver may grant there, `hosts:admin` included for a super-admin.

url.description: Watch and drive the sandbox's Chromium in a browser.

cdpUrl.description: A Chrome DevTools Protocol WebSocket URL, for Playwright's `connectOverCDP` or Puppeteer.

url.description: The page to frame. It holds its token after `#`, so the token reaches no server; treat the URL as a secret.

endMessage.description: What the page posts to its parent once its stream is over.

accountId.description: The account the call acts in when it names none.

superAdmin.description: Whether the caller may manage the deployment's hosts.

Caller.title: Caller
Caller.description: Who is calling, the accounts they may act in, and the deployment's mode.

CallerApiKey.title: CallerApiKey
CallerApiKey.description: The key the call was signed in with, when it was a key.

stdout.description: Its output so far, up to 1 MiB; `truncated` says if there was more.

total.description: What it has cost so far, in `currency`.

ratePerHour.description: What an hour of running costs at its size, in `currency`.

Cost.title: Cost
Cost.description: What a sandbox costs at the deployment's rates. A self-hosted install's rates are 0 unless its operator sets them.

account.description: The account to act in: the caller's personal account (the default for a person) or an organisation they belong to. An API key always acts in its own account, and naming another is `forbidden`.

name.description: The host's name. Default: the machine's hostname.

account.description: The account to act in: the caller's personal account (the default for a person) or an organisation they belong to. An API key always acts in its own account, and naming another is `forbidden`.

CreateApiKeyBody.title: CreateApiKeyBody
CreateApiKeyBody.description: Give `scopes` or a `preset` (or both, which adds them). A key can't hold a scope its maker lacks.

id.description: The user's or the API key's ID.

account.description: The account to act in: the caller's personal account (the default for a person) or an organisation they belong to. An API key always acts in its own account, and naming another is `forbidden`.

name.description: Unique in the account: lower-case letters, digits and dashes, at most 63.

email.description: Only this person may use it. Absent: anyone with the code.

name.description: The project's name, trimmed: not empty, and at most 100 characters.

CreateProjectBody.title: CreateProjectBody
CreateProjectBody.description: Any other field is refused as `invalid`.

account.description: The account to act in: the caller's personal account (the default for a person) or an organisation they belong to. An API key always acts in its own account, and naming another is `forbidden`.

name.description: Default: a generated name, such as `brave-otter`.

image.description: A microVM's base image. Default: the deployment's.

from.description: Start from this snapshot: a snapshot's ID or a saved snapshot's name in the account.

env.description: Environment variables every command sees, after the environment's. Not secrets: they are shown to anyone who may exec. Kantel's own names (`KANTEL_*`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY`, in any case) are refused.

environment.description: Start with this environment, an environment's ID or name in the account: its plain variables, a placeholder for each protected one, its secret files and repositories, and its grants. `env` may not name one of its protected variables.

hostLabels.description: Place it only on a host with each label, such as `{ site: "home" }`.

wait.description: Answer once it is `running` (or `error`) rather than as soon as it is placed.

CreateSandboxBody.title: CreateSandboxBody
CreateSandboxBody.description: Every field is optional: `{}` makes a running isolate in the caller's account.

account.description: The account to act in: the caller's personal account (the default for a person) or an organisation they belong to. An API key always acts in its own account, and naming another is `forbidden`.

url.description: HTTPS; a self-hosted install may allow `http://` to a private address.

DeploymentMode.title: DeploymentMode
DeploymentMode.description: `selfhosted`: an install someone runs for themselves. `hosted`: a hosted service with plans.

url.description: Opens the desktop in a browser. Anyone holding it may use it until it expires.

host.description: The host, on port 443: `api.github.com`, or `*.example.com` for its subdomains (not `example.com` itself).

pathPrefixes.description: Only paths under these, such as `/repos/`. Absent or empty: any path.

items.description: An HTTP method in capitals, such as `GET` or `POST`.

methods.description: Only these methods. Absent or empty: any method.

DestinationBinding.title: DestinationBinding
DestinationBinding.description: Where a protected variable's value may go: the host's egress proxy swaps the sandbox's placeholder for the value only on a request that matches, and refuses a request that carries the placeholder anywhere else.

deviceCode.description: `kdc_…`: the device's secret, which it polls with. Never show it.

userCode.description: `ABCD-EFGH`: the code the person checks in the browser.

verificationUrl.description: The console's page where a signed-in person approves it.

verificationUrlComplete.description: The same page with the code filled in.

intervalSeconds.description: Poll no more often than this.

DeviceLogin.title: DeviceLogin
DeviceLogin.description: A sign-in in the browser under way, as RFC 8628's device authorisation grant.

DeviceLoginRequest.title: DeviceLoginRequest
DeviceLoginRequest.description: A device waiting for a person to approve it, as the approval page shows it.

DeviceLoginResult.title: DeviceLoginResult
DeviceLoginResult.description: With `approved`, the new key and its secret, shown this once.

DeviceLoginState.title: DeviceLoginState
DeviceLoginState.description: `pending`: no one has approved it yet. `approved`: the poll that sees it first gets the key; later polls are `expired`. `denied`: the person refused it. `expired`: too late, or already collected.

url.description: A WebSocket URL to the sandbox's host that carries a Noise session as binary frames. The gateway relays it and can't read it: the device checks the host's key against the space's chain, and the host checks the device's.

hostId.description: The host the sandbox is on: the chain's entry for it has its key.

accountId.description: The sandbox's organisation: the space whose chain the session is in.

ttlMinutes.description: How long a session can be started with this URL; one started in time stays open. Default 10.

user.description: The person whose device will open the session. Refused (`forbidden`) unless the call is that person's, so a browser whose sign-in may have changed under it (a cookie it can't read) never gets a URL for someone else's sign-in to use with its keys.

entries.description: Oldest first; an entry's `seq` is its index.

from.description: The seq of the first entry given: the chain's length as the caller last saw it.

payload.description: Base64url of the entry's JSON, exactly the bytes that were signed.

method.description: `CONNECT` for a tunnel the proxy didn't look inside.

path.description: The path, when the proxy saw it (plain HTTP or inspected HTTPS); never the query.

reason.description: Why it was denied, or what failed, in words.

rule.description: The rule that decided it, such as `deny DELETE api.github.com /repos/*`.

swapped.description: The protected variables whose values the proxy put in, by name.

inspected.description: Whether the proxy looked inside the HTTPS.

status.description: The answer's status, when the proxy saw one.

EgressEntry.title: EgressEntry
EgressEntry.description: One request or connection a sandbox made through its host's egress proxy. Never a value.

host.description: The host: `api.github.com`, or `*.example.com` for its subdomains (not `example.com` itself).

items.description: An HTTP method in capitals, such as `GET` or `POST`.

methods.description: Only these methods. Absent or empty: every method.

paths.description: Path patterns, `*` one segment and `**` the rest, such as `/repos/lleverage-ai/*`. Absent or empty: every path.

EgressGrant.title: EgressGrant
EgressGrant.description: An egress rule on top of the account's proxy settings: let a sandbox reach a host, or refuse it. Deny wins. A grant naming methods or paths makes the proxy look inside that host's HTTPS, as a protected variable's host does.

id.description: Keep a grant's ID; absent, a new one is made.

host.description: The host: `api.github.com`, or `*.example.com` for its subdomains (not `example.com` itself).

items.description: An HTTP method in capitals, such as `GET` or `POST`.

methods.description: Only these methods. Absent or empty: every method.

paths.description: Path patterns, `*` one segment and `**` the rest, such as `/repos/lleverage-ai/*`. Absent or empty: every path.

mode.description: `live`: the open browser as it is now, watch-only. `replay`: its recording.

minutes.description: How long the link lasts. Default 15.

sandboxCount.description: How many sandboxes were made from it and still exist.

Environment.title: Environment
Environment.description: What a sandbox starts with: variables, secret files, repositories and egress grants. A change reaches sandboxes made after it, except a protected variable's value, bindings and the grants, which reach running ones at once.

EnvironmentFile.title: EnvironmentFile
EnvironmentFile.description: A secret file every new sandbox starts with. Its contents are write-only, and kept encrypted.

url.description: HTTPS with no credentials in it, such as `https://github.com/lleverage-ai/kantel`.

ref.description: A branch or tag; default the repository's default branch.

EnvironmentRepo.title: EnvironmentRepo
EnvironmentRepo.description: A repository every new sandbox starts with, cloned through the egress proxy once it is running.

protected.description: A protected variable is a `kph_` placeholder in the sandbox, its own per sandbox, which the host's egress proxy swaps for the value on requests to its bindings: the value never enters the sandbox.

value.description: A plain variable's value. Never answered for a protected one.

bindings.description: A protected variable's destinations, at least one. Empty for a plain one.

ErrorBody.title: ErrorBody
ErrorBody.description: Every error: the KantelError's code and message.

id.description: The event's ID, such as `evt_8x7w6v`: a webhook's delivery ID, so deduplicate on it.

Event.title: Event
Event.description: Something that happened in an account: what webhooks deliver and the history shows.

EventType.title: EventType
EventType.description: `sandbox.created`: made, before it runs. `sandbox.running`: it runs commands now, after a create, resume, fork or recovery. `sandbox.stopped`, `sandbox.paused`: it stopped (by a call or its auto-stop), or paused. `sandbox.error`: it entered `error`. `sandbox.degraded`, `sandbox.recovered`: its host lost and regained it; `sandbox.degraded` also when its environment's secret file or repository couldn't be set up (its reason says which), which leaves it running. `sandbox.deleted`: erased. `snapshot.saved`, `snapshot.deleted`: a saved snapshot was made or deleted.

url.description: Its HTTPS URL. Unless `public`, the answer to exposing it carries a token anyone holding it may use, shown only then (Kantel keeps its hash); listed, the URL has none. Exposing the port again gives a new token and ends the old. Access through it ends when the key or sign-in that exposed it loses access to the sandbox.

public.description: Anyone with the URL may open it, with no token. Default false.

content.description: The file, or with `offset` or `length`, the part read.

size.description: The whole file's size in bytes.

offset.description: With `offset` or `length`: the byte `content` starts at. At `size`, it's empty.

FileContent.title: FileContent
FileContent.description: A file of at most 1 MiB, or a part of at most 1 MiB of a larger one, read with `offset` and `length`.

snapshotId.description: Fork from this snapshot of the sandbox. Default: its newest, or its live state.

injected.description: Kantel put its guest agent into the image at boot (any Linux image), rather than the image shipping it.

arch.description: The machine, as `uname -m` says it: `x86_64` or `aarch64`.

libc.description: The image's C library; `none` for a static userland such as busybox's.

shell.description: The shell a `command` runs in, such as `/bin/bash`; absent: `argv` only.

init.description: PID 1: the image's systemd, or Kantel's own init when the image has none.

GuestCapabilities.title: GuestCapabilities
GuestCapabilities.description: What a microVM's image has, as its guest agent found it when it last started: its OS, and whether it has a desktop, a browser and Docker.

detail.description: What the guest agent found, such as `Xtigervnc, xfce4-session, Selkies`.

reason.description: Why it isn't available, in words, such as `No desktop in this image`.

kvm.description: `/dev/kvm` opens inside, so containers and VMs in it can nest.

detail.description: What the guest agent found, such as `Xtigervnc, xfce4-session, Selkies`.

reason.description: Why it isn't available, in words, such as `No desktop in this image`.

GuestFeature.title: GuestFeature
GuestFeature.description: One thing a microVM's image has or lacks.

name.description: Its pretty name, such as `Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie)`.

latestVersion.description: The newest version the control plane offers.

accountId.description: The account the host belongs to, when it was added to one by its people: only that account's sandboxes run on it. Absent for a host the deployment's super-admin joined, which any account's sandboxes may use.

Host.title: Host
Host.description: A machine that runs sandboxes. It dials out to the control plane; it takes no inbound ports.

token.description: `kth_…`, shown once. It joins one host.

command.description: The one-line command that installs and registers a host with it.

HostState.title: HostState
HostState.description: `online`: connected and taking sandboxes. `unreachable`: its connection dropped; its sandboxes can't be reached until it is back. `draining`: connected, but takes no new sandboxes. `revoked`: its credential is revoked.

code.description: The join code, such as `kji_…`. Shown once, when the invite is made.

Invite.title: Invite
Invite.description: A way into an organisation: whoever joins with its code becomes a member.

secret.description: The key itself, `ksk_…`. Shown once: store it now.

MemberRole.title: MemberRole
MemberRole.description: `member`: uses the organisation's shared sandboxes and snapshots and makes their own. `admin`: also manages members, API keys, webhooks, telemetry and the proxy. `owner`: also renames or deletes the organisation. A personal account's person is its `owner`.

organisationId.description: The organisation the project is in: always the caller's.

enabled.description: Send sandboxes' outbound traffic through the proxy.

defaultAction.description: What happens to a host no rule names.

deny.description: Hosts always refused; deny wins over allow.

attribution.description: Tell the upstream which sandbox and account each request came from, in signed `Kantel-Sandbox` and `Kantel-Account` headers.

ProxySettings.title: ProxySettings
ProxySettings.description: Where sandboxes' outbound traffic may go, and through what, for one account. Experimental.

ProxySettingsExpected.title: ProxySettingsExpected
ProxySettingsExpected.description: The settings as you last read them: `GET /proxy`'s answer will do. Given, the write is refused with `conflict` if they have changed since, so an edit made from an older read can't undo someone else's: read them again and redo the edit. Left out, the settings are replaced whatever they hold.

url.description: Another proxy every allowed request goes on to, such as a Mehen.

headerNames.description: The names of the headers Kantel sends it; their values are never shown.

expected.description: The list as you last read it. Given, the write is refused with `conflict` if the list has changed since, so an edit made from an older read can't undo someone else's: read it again and redo the edit. Left out, the list is replaced whatever it holds.

The list as you last read it. Given, the write is refused with `conflict` if the list has changed since, so an edit made from an older read can't undo someone else's: read it again and redo the edit. Left out, the list is replaced whatever it holds.

account.description: The account to act in: the caller's personal account (the default for a person) or an organisation they belong to. An API key always acts in its own account, and naming another is `forbidden`.
The account to act in: the caller's personal account (the default for a person) or an organisation they belong to. An API key always acts in its own account, and naming another is `forbidden`.

command.description: A shell command line, run with `bash -lc` (or the isolate's shell).

detached.description: Start it and answer at once, with no time limit; read it back by its ID.

subdomain.description: Its name under the deployment's sandbox domain, which its public port URLs start with.

image.description: The base image a microVM was made from, such as `ubuntu-24.04`.

reason.description: Why it is in `error` or `degraded`, in words.

autoStopMinutes.description: How long after a start or resume it stops by itself; `null` never.

stopsAt.description: When it will stop by itself, while running; the console's stops-in.

latestSnapshotId.description: The snapshot a resume or fork would use.

environmentId.description: The environment it was made from.

grants.description: Its own egress grants, on top of its environment's.

hostId.description: The host it runs on; only a super-admin is shown it.

pause.description: Whether it can be paused with its memory kept.

SandboxCapabilities.title: SandboxCapabilities
SandboxCapabilities.description: What this sandbox can do, from its type and its host, and for a microVM from what its guest agent found in its image (`guest`): `desktop`, `browser`, `docker` and `kvm` are false where the image lacks them.

environmentGrants.description: Its environment's grants, which it has too.

grants.description: Its own grants, on top of its environment's.

entries.description: Newest first; Kantel keeps the newest 1000.

SandboxEgress.title: SandboxEgress
SandboxEgress.description: A sandbox's egress: what it was made with, its own grants and its log.

SandboxHealth.title: SandboxHealth
SandboxHealth.description: `degraded`: the machine is up but its host can't fully reach it; it keeps running.

placeholderPrefix.description: The first 8 characters of its placeholder, such as `kph_7Qx2`.

SandboxProtectedVariable.title: SandboxProtectedVariable
SandboxProtectedVariable.description: A protected variable as one sandbox has it: never its value.

SandboxSizeName.title: SandboxSizeName
SandboxSizeName.description: A microVM's size; a deployment may offer fewer. Isolates have none.

sandboxId.description: Set when it was forked from another sandbox.

SandboxState.title: SandboxState
SandboxState.description: `starting`: being placed and booted. `running`: commands run now. `stopping`: its disk is being saved. `stopped`: no machine; its disk is kept as its newest snapshot, and running programs are gone. `paused`: like `stopped`, but its memory is kept too, so `resume` carries on where it left off (microVMs only). `error`: the last operation failed or the machine was lost; `recover` or `resume` it. `deleting`, `deleted`: erased for good, with its snapshots.

SandboxType.title: SandboxType
SandboxType.description: `isolate`: a workerd isolate with a JavaScript shell over the sandbox's files. Starts in milliseconds and costs almost nothing, but runs no native binaries, has no desktop and no SSH. `microvm`: a Firecracker microVM with a full Linux, root, Docker and `/dev/kvm` inside, a desktop, a browser and SSH.

SandboxVisibility.title: SandboxVisibility
SandboxVisibility.description: `private`: only the person who made it (and API keys of theirs) may see or use it. `organisation`: every member of its organisation may. A personal account's sandboxes are always `private`.

sandboxId.description: The sandbox to save, running or stopped.

snapshotId.description: Save this snapshot of the sandbox's history. Default: its state now.

replace.description: Replace a saved snapshot of the same name.

content.description: At most 1 MiB, in `encoding`. Required for a new file; left out, the file keeps its contents.

SetEnvironmentFileBody.title: SetEnvironmentFileBody
SetEnvironmentFileBody.description: `encoding` says how `content` is written: `utf8` (the default) or `base64`.

value.description: Required for a new variable and when it becomes protected or plain. Left out on a protected one, it keeps its value (to change its bindings); a new value for a protected one is a rotation.

bindings.description: A protected variable's destinations, at least one. Left out, a protected one keeps its own.

name.description: A saved snapshot's name, unique in its account.

sandboxId.description: The sandbox it was taken of; absent once that is deleted.

memory.description: Whether it holds the sandbox's memory as well as its disk (a pause).

SnapshotKind.title: SnapshotKind
SnapshotKind.description: `automatic`: one of a sandbox's own history, taken as it runs and at each stop; the newest is what a resume or fork uses, and older ones expire. `saved`: kept under a name until deleted, and usable as a template for new sandboxes, even after its sandbox is deleted.

user.description: Names the sandbox to the gateway.

command.description: A command line that connects, such as `ssh -p 2222 sbx_4kq9x2mt@ssh.example`.

proxyUrl.description: When there is no SSH gateway to dial: a WebSocket URL carrying the sandbox's SSH as binary frames, for an `ssh -o ProxyCommand=…` (`kantel ssh-proxy` is one). Anyone holding it can start a connection until `expiresAt`.

privateKey.description: When Kantel made the key pair: its private key, shown once.

publicKey.description: An OpenSSH public key to let in. Absent: Kantel makes a key pair for this access.

ttlMinutes.description: How long a connection can be started with this access; one started in time stays open. Default 10.

clientName.description: What is signing in, shown to the person who approves it and given to its key: `kantel on build-01`.

keepMemory.description: Pause instead: keep its memory as well as its disk (`paused`). microVMs only. Default false.

endpoint.description: An OTLP/HTTP collector's base URL; `/v1/metrics` and `/v1/logs` are added.

headerNames.description: The headers sent with each export; values never shown.

TelemetryExport.title: TelemetryExport
TelemetryExport.description: Where an account's telemetry goes: sandbox metrics (`kantel.sandbox.running`, `kantel.sandbox.cpu.seconds`, `kantel.sandbox.cost`, …) every 60 seconds, and each lifecycle event as an OTLP log record when it happens.

TelemetryTestResult.title: TelemetryTestResult
TelemetryTestResult.description: What the collector answered to an empty export sent on save.

draining.description: Stop placing new sandboxes on it.

extendMinutes.description: Move `stopsAt` to this long from now.

recentCpu.description: CPU utilisation, 0 to 1, over the last 24 intervals of 5 minutes, oldest first: a sparkline.

viewOnly.description: Watch only: no keyboard or mouse. Default false.

ttlMinutes.description: How long the URLs can be opened for; a view or connection opened in time stays open. Default 10.

Webhook.title: Webhook
Webhook.description: An HTTPS endpoint that gets an account's events, signed as Standard Webhooks are: `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` and `webhook-signature` (`v1,` and the base64 HMAC-SHA256 of `id.timestamp.body`, keyed by the secret after its `whsec_`). Failed deliveries are retried with backoff, up to 8 attempts.
